title: Text pair for Q7: The Lens and Letter on the Railway
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 55 (Text pair 'The Lens' and 'Letter on the Railway' (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 55: Two extracts under time: the 15-mark Q7 comparison. Teacher-written for TGA. Read, then answer under time.

passage.title: Text One: The Lens
paras: The lighthouse keeper's cottage is a museum now. You pay at a little window and climb the same hundred and twelve steps he climbed each night, though nobody makes you do it in a gale. At the top, behind glass, sits the great lens: a beehive of prisms taller than a man, so clean it seems to hold the sky. A card explains how it turned on a bath of mercury, so smoothly that a child could push it. I did push it, very gently, when the guide was not looking. It moved. Somewhere, two hundred years of ships seemed to move with it.

passage.title: Text Two: Letter on the Railway
paras: Dear Mother, The railway has reached our town at last, and with it a noise I am not sure we shall ever grow used to. On Tuesday the first engine came in, breathing fire and steam like a creature from one of Father's old books. Half the town ran to the station; the other half ran away from it. The baker's horse broke its rope and was found two fields off, eating Mr Hale's cabbages. I confess I stood very near the platform's edge, and when the great wheels stopped I felt my heart had been running all the way from London with it.

questions.q: Q7. Compare how the writers present their experiences. Support your answer with detail from both texts.
questions.a: Shared awe and daring ('I did push it' / 'very near the platform's edge'); a modern visitor to history versus a nineteenth-century witness of something new; the beehive metaphor and the creature 'breathing fire'; confessional first person; both end in personal feeling; integrated with connectives and a judgement.

questions.q: Fill the plan grid with one more idea
questions.a: For example: the effect on other people: the guide versus the whole town.
For example: 'The lens is calm and still, whereas the engine is loud and alive.'

questions.q: Core (timed, 20 minutes): in the portal response box, answer Q7. Starter: 'Both writers...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: shared awe and daring; perspective of a modern visitor to history versus a nineteenth-century witness of something new; methods: metaphor of the beehive and the creature; confessional first person; structure ending in personal feeling; integrated with connectives and a judgement.

questions.a: For example: the letter-writer has never seen a machine move without a horse.
